record.paper_title: QED: An Open-Source Multi-Agent System for Generating Mathematical Proofs on Open Problems
record.original_question: On the two-dimensional torus T² = [−π, π]², with functions periodic in both variables with period 2π, does there exist a nonzero smooth mean-zero initial scalar θ₀(x,y) and a shear velocity field u(y,t) in L∞ in time with W^{1,1} regularity in y, satisfying ∫_T |∂_y u(y,t)| dy ≤ C, such that the solution of the transport equation θ_t + u(y,t) ∂_x θ = 0 with θ(x,y,0)=θ₀(x,y) has homogeneous H^{-1} norm bounded by C₁ e^{−C₂ t} for some constants C₁,C₂>0? Equivalently, prove either that such exponential mixing is possible or that it is impossible under these assumptions, where the homogeneous H^{-1} norm is defined by summing |θ̂(n)|²/|n|² over nonzero Fourier modes n in Z² and θ̂(n)=∫_{T²} θ(x,y)e^{−i n·(x,y)} dx dy.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Can you find a nonzero function θ0(x, y) ∈ C∞(T2) such that ∫ T2 θ0(x, y) dx dy = 0, and there exists a velocity field u(y, t) ∈ L∞ t W1,1 y (T), that is, ∫ T |∂yu(y, t)| dy ≤ C for some constant C, satisfying the following: For the initial value problem θt + u(y, t) ∂xθ = 0, θ(x, y, 0) = θ0(x, y), (1) the solution satisfies ∥θ(t)∥H˙ −1(T2) ≤ C1e−C2t (2) for some constants C1, C2 > 0.

Here the homogeneous H˙ −1 norm is defined by ∥θ(t)∥2 H˙ −1(T2) = ∑ n∈Z2 |n|>0 1 |n|2 |θˆ(n)|2, where the Fourier coefficient θˆ(n) is given by θˆ(n) = ∫ T2 θ(x, y) e−in·(x,y) dx dy. Or, on the contrary, prove that this is not possible. Result. QED proved that exponential mixing is impossible under these conditions in Round 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^2 = [-\pi,\pi]^2$ be the two-dimensional torus, with all functions assumed $2\pi$-periodic in each variable. For a function $\theta\in L^2(\mathbb{T}^2)$ define the Fourier coefficients
$$\hat\theta(n) = \int_{\mathbb{T}^2} \theta(x,y)\, e^{-i n\cdot (x,y)}\, dx\, dy, \qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}^2,$$
and the homogeneous $\dot H^{-1}$ norm by
$$\|\theta\|_{\dot H^{-1}(\mathbb{T}^2)}^2 = \sum_{\substack{n\in\mathbb{Z}^2\\ |n|>0}} \frac{|\hat\theta(n)|^2}{|n|^2}.$$
Determine whether there exist:
(i) a nonzero function $\theta_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^2)$ with $\int_{\mathbb{T}^2}\theta_0(x,y)\,dx\,dy = 0$,
(ii) a shear velocity field $u(y,t)\in L^\infty_t W^{1,1}_y(\mathbb{T})$, that is, a measurable function $u:\mathbb{T}\times[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying $\int_{\mathbb{T}} |\partial_y u(y,t)|\,dy \le C$ for some constant $C$ uniformly in $t$,
such that the unique solution $\theta(x,y,t)$ of the transport equation
$$\partial_t \theta + u(y,t)\,\partial_x\theta = 0, \qquad \theta(x,y,0) = \theta_0(x,y)$$
satisfies
$$\|\theta(\,\cdot\,,t)\|_{\dot H^{-1}(\mathbb{T}^2)} \le C_1\, e^{-C_2 t}\qquad \text{for all } t\ge 0,$$
for some constants $C_1, C_2 > 0$. Prove either that such a configuration exists, or that no such $(\theta_0, u)$ can exist.
artifact.status_search_result: It is classical that a pure shear velocity field $u(y,t)\partial_x$ cannot mix exponentially: the solution is $\theta(x,y,t)=\theta_0(x-\int_0^t u(y,s)\,ds, y)$, and the $y$-profile of each Fourier mode in $x$ is preserved, so the decay of $\|\theta(t)\|_{\dot H^{-1}}$ is at most algebraic (typically $t^{-1/2}$) under bounded variation/$W^{1,1}$ control on $u$. Recent work on "Exponential Mixing by Shear Flows" achieves exponential mixing only by alternating horizontal and vertical shears, not a single shear in $y$. Thus exponential mixing is impossible under the stated single-direction shear and $W^{1,1}_y$ assumption.

status_evidence.title: Exponential Mixing by Shear Flows (SIAM J. Math. Anal.)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs exponentially mixing flows by alternating horizontal and vertical shears, indicating that a single-direction shear with BV/W^{1,1} regularity does not exponentially mix.
status_evidence.claim: Exponential mixing for shear-type flows requires alternation between two shear directions; pure one-direction shears do not achieve exponential decay of \dot H^{-1}.

status_evidence.title: Numerical Evidence of Exponential Mixing by Alternating Shear Flows (arXiv:2111.00093)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies alternating horizontal/vertical shears, suggesting exponential mixing requires both directions.
status_evidence.claim: A single shear u(y,t)\partial_x cannot produce exponential mixing on \mathbb{T}^2.
